what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/form-groups-and-matches: keep groups of anything in a person's records, regroup a tree, and form matches and groups of people by grounded expected value with consent before any introduction.

payload.label: Read my groups and everything inside them
payload.job: Show what is in my groups, lists or collections, with the groups inside them, in their order
payload.description: Give roots: the addresses of the groups to start from, each { family, parts: { name: text } }. Each group is read from the person's records (type group) and every member that is itself a group is followed, so the answer holds those groups and everything inside them at any depth. Returns groups (each { groupRef, memberOrder, members: { memberId: { memberId, nodeRef, role?, presentation? } } }, members in memberOrder), count, and skipped: the ids of records that were not a well-formed group or claimed another group's address. A root that is not a group yet is simply not in the answer. It changes nothing.

provenance.source: ported from the group package (membership graph, its record fold and its reachable-groups read), to the records door

payload.label: Change my groups: add, move, order, nest and remove
payload.job: Add things to my groups, lists or collections, move and reorder them, put some into a new group inside, take a group apart, or bring a whole folder tree in as groups
payload.description: A group is any list of addresses (records, pages, people, other groups) in an order; a member whose address is a group nests that group. changes is a list applied in order as one change: ensure-group, add-member (nodeRef, memberId, role?, presentation?, placement?), remove-member (memberId), reorder-member (memberId, placement), move-member (memberId, toGroupRef, placement?), set-member-fields (memberId, role and presentation, null clears), patch-member-presentation (memberId, presentation merged into what is there), group-members (memberIds, toGroupRef: the new group, wrapperMemberId), ungroup-members (wrapperMemberId), delete-group. Every change names groupRef { family, parts }; a placement is { index }, { before: memberId }, { after: memberId } or { at: start | end }. Member ids are yours: nothing is invented. tree (optional) is { family, records: [{ node_id, parent_id, ordinal, role, title, external_identity, attributes }] }: nodes with role group become groups and every node is placed in its parent by ordinal, its title and attributes kept as presentation. The groups touched are read first; a group can never end up inside itself, and a repeated member id is refused, so the whole change is refused and nothing is written. Only groups that changed are written; a group that is gone is removed. Returns groups (every group the change read or made, as it is now), written, removed (record ids) and unplaced (tree nodes not placed, with why).

provenance.source: ported from the group package (membership operations, the containment-tree bridge and the minimal write set), to the records door

payload.label: Regroup a folder tree the way I say, or turn it into groups
payload.job: Move folders under other folders by their names, the way I describe it, or turn a tree of folders into groups
payload.description: records is the tree as flat records { node_id, parent_id (null for a root), ordinal, role, title, external_identity, attributes }; a node with role group holds others. operation nest-by-intent takes intent { nest: [{ parent_title, child_titles }], scope?: { root_node_id?, applies_to_role?, depth? }, materialize_missing_parents?: { kind } }: titles are matched without case or outer spaces, only the named nodes move, two nodes with one title are a refusal for that row and never a guess, a missing parent is made only when materialize_missing_parents is given (its id from new_parent_ids[title] when you give one), and a row that would put a group inside itself is refused; every other row still applies. Returns records (the tree after), moved, created, refusals ({ row, reason, detail }) and untouched. operation tree-to-groups takes family and returns groups, unplaced (with why), group_count and member_count. It writes nothing: tool:change-my-groups keeps a tree as groups.

provenance.source: ported from the group package (grouping intent over a containment tree, and the tree-to-groups bridge)

payload.label: Form matches and small groups by grounded expected value
payload.job: Match people in a community, club, cohort or mentoring program into pairs or small groups who can actually help each other, and prepare introductions that wait for everyone's consent
payload.description: One matching cycle, all of it data: expected_value { factors, scope_fields, minimum_expected_value?, minimum_distinguishable_delta?, require_scope? } names what a match's value is the product of and what scope it is for. Give retrieval_results (one row per subject: { subject, shortlist: [candidates] }, cut to retrieval.shortlist_size each, so work is subjects x shortlist size) or scored candidates. Every candidate needs factor_evidence: a grounded bundle (tool:check-match-evidence) with a score in (0, 1], evidence and an inference for every factor; a candidate without it, or with a value that is not the exact product, forms no group. Similarity from a search only breaks ties. pairing sets group_size, minimum_group_size, include_subject, bipartite roles, exclusion of pairs already met (already_matched, or prior_items), exclusive_participation and names for group sizes. Each group carries a prepared introduction whose send gate is ready only when initiative.required_level is in initiative.pre_authorized_levels and every party's own consent value is in consent_policy.approved_values with no veto in veto_values; connections are given only for those. Returns connections (with relationship_kind), groups, introductions (ready and blocked), reasoning_requests for the chosen few only, configuration_requests, pair_keys, unmatched with details, and how much work was done. Nothing is sent or written.

provenance.source: ported from the interaction-program package (bounded shortlists, expected-value grouping, consent-gated introductions)

payload.label: Check that a match rests on what people actually said
payload.job: Turn people's intake answers into scoped profiles and check that a proposed match's scores cite what both people actually said before anyone is matched
payload.description: Everything about the intake is the contract you give: factors, primitives, scope_fields, questions [{ question_id, claim_kinds, primitive_ids, scope_field? }], citation_requirements per factor [{ side: subject | candidate, any_of: [claim kinds] }], authority [{ name, claim_kind, list? }] and forbidden_interventions (the authority entry whose values block a proposal). operation build-profile takes participant_ref, answer_facts [{ question_id, answer_fact_ref, value, evidence_refs? }] and connected_source_facts (each must carry its consent, access lease, field scope, observation and expiry times and whether it can be revoked, or it is not evidence) and returns the profile: claims, the scope, coverage per primitive, authority, status grounded or partial, and problems. operation check-assessment takes subject_profile, candidate_profile, assessments (per factor: score in (0, 1], rationale, inference_ref, the claim refs it cites on each side and evidence_refs) and proposed_interventions, and returns per-factor evidence with status grounded or no_justified_match and the reasons; a proposal either person forbids blocks every factor. Nothing here scores: scores come from whoever assessed, and only cited ones pass.

provenance.source: ported from the interaction-program package (match intake evidence and grounded factor evidence), its question contract made an input

payload.label: Assign helpers to the people who need them, within each helper's capacity
payload.job: Assign mentors, volunteers or helpers to the people who asked for help when each helper can only take so many, best pairs first, and say who was left without one and why
payload.description: operation solve_capacity_constraints takes help_seekers [{ id, match_case_id?, demand? }], helper_candidates [{ id, capacity_ref?, session_ref?, mode? }], capacities (by helper id, or a list in helper id order), and your answers about pairs: eligibility [{ help_seeker_ref, helper_candidate_ref, eligible, reason? }] and ranking [{ help_seeker_ref, helper_candidate_ref, score, explanation? }]. The best-ranked eligible pairs are taken first; a helper is never booked past capacity and nobody is assigned to themself. operation solve_expected_value_capacity_constraints takes scored candidates (as for tool:form-matches) with expected_value, group_size, capacities and exclusive_participation, and needs a clear cut after each seeker's demand. propose_assignment turns a solved answer into proposals; record_outcome records outcome_fact_refs for one assignment_proposal. Returns assignments (state proposed), unmatched (with reason: capacity_exhausted, no_eligible_helper, indistinguishable_expected_value, ...), capacity_usage and how much work was done. Rounds that swap who helps and who is helped are two requests.

provenance.source: ported from the interaction-program package (capacity-constrained assignment), its predicate and ranking functions made pair answers

payload.label: Choose which options go ahead together
payload.job: Choose which of several options (a person, a workflow, a tool, a place) go ahead now: every worthwhile one that does not compete for the same thing, the best where they do
payload.description: configurations [{ id, configuration_kind (any word), expected_value, scope: { <field>: text }, required_resource_refs?, collision_refs? }] and scope_fields (the scope every configuration must name). Every configuration with a positive value and a complete scope goes ahead at the same time; two compete only when they share a collision ref, and then the higher value wins. Two that share a collision ref and are within minimum_distinguishable_delta of each other are both held back rather than picked between. Returns selected, rejected (with reason: non_positive_expected_value, scope_missing, resource_collision, indistinguishable_expected_value, ...), configuration_requests (state proposed) and counts.

provenance.source: ported from the interaction-program package (configuration selection above pairing)

payload.label: Run a community's matchmaker clock: start or close a round, introduce, follow up
payload.job: Pair a community's members on its cadence without anyone asking: start a round when it is due, close it at its deadline, make introductions everyone said yes to, and follow up the ones nobody acted on
payload.description: The wake target of a community's matchmaker; a person declares it as their own wake (a wake-declaration record with tool tool:advance-a-community-matchmaker, a time repeat, and input { community_id }). Reads the community's settings (a match-community record, checked by tool:check-community-matching-settings), its members, rounds, matches and answers. When no round is open and the cadence (every_days after the last round) has come, it starts one: each opted-in member whose answers are incomplete gets a profile job for their own AI, and each complete member gets a bounded shortlist (an inverted index over categories and words, at most shortlist_size candidates, never every pair) and a score job asking their AI to score each candidate on the contract's factors with cited claims. Nothing here runs a model. At the deadline it forms groups from the grounded scores only (exact product of the factors, every factor cited), proposes each and hands each person's AI a consent job. It makes the one-to-one group of any match whose yeses all hold and hands topic jobs; it hands follow-up jobs at the community's follow_up_hours until the members talk. Jobs are ai-job records on the engine's job road, once per request key. Returns round (what started or closed, or null), next_at (when the clock next has something to do) and written; a community without usable settings returns ok false and its error.

community_id.description: The community whose matchmaker runs: its settings are the match-community record of this id.

now.description: The time to run at, in milliseconds or ISO words; left out, the time of the run.

provenance.source: ported from the community matchmaker of the Trillion app (src/community-matching.mjs, its introduction states and consent fingerprint) onto the matching leaves of this folder and the records door

payload.label: Answer a community's matchmaker: profile, scores, yes or no, topics, wrote
payload.job: Give a community's matchmaker what it asked for: a member's answers and on/off switch, an AI's cited scores for its shortlist, a person's yes or no to an introduction, first topics, or that they wrote in the one-to-one
payload.description: One answer from one person (person), then the community's clock. kind profile: { on?, answers: { question_id: answer }, categories? }, refused when a question is not one the community asks or an answer holds the community's contact pattern. kind scores: { round_id, scores: [{ candidate_ref, factors: { factor: { score in (0, 1], reason, you: [claim_ref], them: [claim_ref] } } }] }; answers which candidates were grounded and why not, and the round closes once every asked AI answered. kind answer: { match_id, yes, consent }: a yes counts only when the answer carries the community's person stamp (consent.yes_needs) and the consent the person was shown (read-my-community-matches gives it); an AI's yes is refused with the screen to open; a no, from the person or their AI, passes the match for everyone. Once every member's yes holds, the one-to-one group (group:introduction) is made and each AI is asked for first topics. kind topics: { match_id, topics: [line] }. kind wrote: { match_id }: once every member wrote, the match has talked. kind run-round: the community's owner closes the open round and starts the next. Returns outcome ({ ok: true, ... } or { ok: false, error, status, next_call?, changed?, consent? }), round, next_at and written.

payload.label: Read my matches in a community, my profile, and the score job I owe
payload.job: See who a community's matchmaker proposed for me and where each introduction stands, what my profile still misses, the shortlist my AI still has to score, and fellow members who share my categories
payload.description: Reads one member's view (person): on (their switch), cadence_label, next_at, matches (each match_id, status and the community's words for it, answered, answer_by, consent: what to answer a yes with, with, why: the scoring AI's cited reasons, topics, space_id once they are in the one-to-one), profile (answers, categories, complete, missing questions), waiting_for_your_scores (the open round's shortlist with citable claims), discover (members sharing a category, with what they offer and seek), waiting_jobs (this person's own waiting jobs, for their AI to pull: nothing is ever written into another person's account), wake_at (when the community's clock next acts, so the member side wakes then and pulls once), and for the community's owner experiments (each arm's introduced and talked counts and the shown and converted events an experiment owner reads). Writes nothing.

payload.label: Forget a person in a community's matchmaker
payload.job: Erase a person from a community's matching: what they told it, every match naming them, their asks, answers and jobs, and their place and scores on other members' shortlists and score jobs
payload.description: Removes the member record, every match naming the person with its one-to-one group, answers and jobs, their own asks and jobs, and takes them and the scores of them out of other members' asks and waiting score jobs. Others keep their own asks and jobs. Returns forgotten and written.

payload.label: Check a community's matchmaker settings before keeping them
payload.job: Check that a community's matching settings can run: cadence, sizes, the evidence contract and the questions that cover every factor's citations, consent, follow-up hours, words for every job, refusal and state, contact pattern, limits and experiments
payload.description: community is the value of a match-community record: { title, owner, created_at, matching }. Returns usable and problems, each a plain sentence naming the field to fix. matching holds every_days, round_hours, shortlist_size, posting_cap, group_size, cadence_label, default_on, contract (the match-evidence contract: factors, primitives, scope_fields, questions, citation_requirements, authority, forbidden_interventions), questions (the contract questions this community asks, which must cover every claim kind a factor cites), expected_value? (minimum_expected_value, minimum_distinguishable_delta), initiative { required_level, pre_authorized_levels }, grouping?, consent { answer_hours, selection { approved_values, veto_values }, yes_needs { field, equals }, screen }, follow_up_hours, jobs (profile, score, consent, topics, follow_up: { said, job } with {name} fields), words, state_words, contact_pattern, limits, discover { offers, seeks } and experiments? ([{ id, arms: [{ id, weight, jobs }] }]). Nothing is written.
